source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Thrips (ថ្រីប, Scirtothrips dorsalis, family Thripidae) are tiny, slender insects that scrape and feed on the surface of young leaves, flowers, and developing fruit rind. Feeding on young fruit causes a characteristic ring of silvery-gray scarring around the stem end of the fruit as it grows and expands, which is a cosmetic defect that lowers the fruit's market grade even though it does not affect the edible flesh.

Because thrips are extremely small and feed in tight spaces such as between touching fruit or under the calyx, they are easy to overlook until scarring is already visible on growing fruit, several weeks after the actual feeding damage occurred.

Management focuses on protecting fruit during the vulnerable early fruit-set period, when the rind is still soft enough to scar, monitoring flowering and early fruit-set closely, and applying control measures at that critical window rather than throughout the season.
